b: ^ Salutations to you, good sir, on this most melancholy of morns! You are the purveyor of the printed word that hast descended upon my most humble abode, I presume?

Start: ^Ms. Tendwell said you were first to discover the body. Is that true?
^Kid, I can't understand a single word you're saying.
^Did your father confiscate your copy of the Iliad.
^It was you! You killed the Admiral!

c-0: ^'Tis true! As Theseus did witness his dear father Aegeus' perilous precipitation from the Acropolis, so too was I first to discover the end of our dear paterfamilias!

^Roused from slumber was I by a most discomfiting cacophony emanating from my progenitor's sanctum. Two voices, both brimming with vexation and trepidation, one clashing 'gainst t'other as Achilles did strike at Hector's shield!
^Compelled was I by divine providence to hasten to my father's side. Alas, I was too late. I came upon my father's bloodied form, his body and spirit cleft in twain, ne'er to be made whole.
^And thus was my juvenescence brought to a tragic close.
c-2: ^Pray tell, what precisely intrigues you so?
c-3: ^Ah, yes. A rare disturbance between my father and I. Most inflamed was I that he would dare deprive me of my most treasured manuscript.
^Yet in light of recent events, it does seem such a petty squabble...
c-4: ^Am I to understand, sir that, you intend to level an accusation of patricide against me?
c-5: ^ You subtly inspect Avery for clues.

Night_Of_Murder: ^So, you went to inspect an argument in your father's study, but he was dead by the time you got there. Is that right?
^Who was at the scene of the crime?
^Was the murderer still in the room?
^Did you notice anything unusual about the body?

c-1:
^Alas, so impassioned had this fatal tête-à-tête become that it had devolved into a deadly conflagration before I could the study.

^Thus the subject matter eluded me. Confound these juvenile feet! Would that I were blessed with the nimble stride of Hermes!
c-2: ^First, Dorothy came to my side, dressed in naught but a nightie! Then came dear Mother, and some time after her, my Dear uncle.
^Ms. Lavender Ditch, devoted ostler to the family horses, was not present.
c-3: ^Yes, although their countenance I could not make out. In the window were they framed, their back turned.
^Naught could I do but watch as the dastardly assailant did defenestrate themselves and abscond into the dark!
c-4: ^Only the familial emblem brazenly torn from the admiralty's coatee. I can only conjecture that the brigand is some sort of larcenist, intent on trafficking our familial coat of arms.
^But to dispatch my noble Father... Would a petty thief truly debauch their mortal souls for mere coin?
c-5: ^As Heracles did heed Eurystheus' deeds, so shall I comply.

Relationship: ^Did you have a happy family life before this?
^Did your father treat the servants kindly?

c-0:
^Icarus was I to my father's Daedalus. Great knowledge did he impart to me. I loved him dearly.

^Alas, a subversion of the tragic tale! 'Tis now my Icarus destined to behold Daedalus' terrible fall!
c-1: ^Ah, so vivid seem those halcyon days of yore! Most ebullient was the noble house of Wenchwatch Hall heretofore. I remember it as though 'twere only yesterday.
^Yes, a most agreeable household. Father & mother did tend to my every need, their happy matrimony the cornerstone of our familial bliss.
^Mother and uncle shared an ardour for the equestrian arts. Their hebdomadary treks astride the stallions in our stables brought them much joy.
^And the fraternal bond between dear father and uncle? 'Twas nigh unshakeable! Often did they exchange good-natured bon mots and rapier repartees! But ne'er could their sibling bond be put asunder.
^Naught but the icy hand of death could accomplish such a feat...
c-2: ^Most propitious were the servile sentiments towards the Admiral. Ne'er once did I hear Ms. Tendwell nor Ms. Ditch speak ill of dear Father, but many's the time did they venerate his good name.
c-3: ^Of course. I shall acquiesce to your every whim.

Call_Dorothy: ^Oft is it that this damnable jejune tongue of mine does confound the guests of Wenchwatch Hall.
^What the hell does that even mean?!
^Why you no speak good English, kid?!

c-0: ^I can only apologise, sir - I will do my best to communicate succinctly.
c-1: ^I do not know, sir! Truly, it is a terrible aggrievement for me as much as you. Confound my lack of oratorical ability!

Crying: ^Wait wait wait! Don't cry! I was only joking, I swear!
^Spare me your crocodile tears, you patricidal maniac! You're going away for a long time!
You_Fucked_Up: ^Sir. I would recommend you cease bothering the young master. Immediately. The young master did not kill his father, as you suggest. He is eight. I will not tolerate further suggestions to the contrary.

c-0: ^'Tis quite alright sir. I am prone to these fulminations of emotion. Such is the malediction of youth.
^ His fingertips seems slightly sticky. You think he may have recently been eating something covered in jam.
c-1: ^ His cheeks are stained red. You think he may have been crying recently.
c-2: ^ He has been dressed in appropriate mourning attire. However, you notice that Avery appears to be carrying something in his back pocket.
^ You think you might be able to grab it, if you're careful...
c-3: ^ You return to your conversation with the unusually verbose child.

Accuse: ^Your father took your book, and you killed him for it! You're going to the gallows, kid!
^I don't know why I think that, but I'll find proof! And then you'll hand, kid!

c-1: ^If this be a jape, 'tis a jape made in remrkably poor taste, sir.
c-2: ^A most difficult charge to pretermit, though I shall do my best.
